about: Every place-specific figure the town generator uses for a small town in Tamil Nadu, India, with its source; where none was found or opened, the source says so (a PLACEHOLDER or 'to confirm'). NOT REPRESENTED YET (the profile structure cannot hold them): informal and own-account work (about nine in ten of India's workers; self-employment earnings and casual labour are read for wages only, and every job here is an employee's job), joint and extended families (they are drawn as 2-3 unrelated adults, so households are smaller than the census's), and the means test on the old-age pension (it is paid to everyone from 60, though in India only the poor are entitled). Also not represented: monthly pay periods (pay is counted in fortnights), the free block of electricity, the tax rebate and cess, and storms concentrated in the northeast monsoon. The census used is 2011, fifteen years old. A world for another place and time is another profile; the platform's code holds none of these (docs/profiles.md). SINCE 2026-10-09 (employment.*): part of the first is represented: registered and unregistered jobs, work by the day, and own-account traders (about 5% of people in work; the other own-account kinds, which are most of them, are still drawn as employees).

sources.culture.conducts: What people start out holding right, for the four conducts where a figure in this profile's own outlook speaks to it (the rest start from values alone: no figure was opened). approves_bps is the national share with 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' of confidence, as `outlook.trust` has it (World Values Survey and European Values Study, joint wave 7, as Our World in Data publishes it; opened 2026-10-11, to confirm against the survey's tables; see sources.outlook for the country and the items). Mapping, ours: answer_tribunal and take_to_tribunal <- confidence in the courts (a person who trusts the courts approves of answering a case there and of taking a wrong to it); complain <- confidence in the civil service (writing to the town is approved where the town's officers are trusted to answer); join_union <- confidence in labour unions. Weak: confidence in an institution is not approval of an act toward it, and the share above a threshold is read as a mean, as outlook does; the figure sets where people start (their own lean and their picture of what others approve), nothing else, and the lean is measured from it, so the rates stay the calibrated ones. No figure for strike, take_in, stay_past_notice, take_from_employer or an organisation's conduct (the survey's items on joining strikes and on the justifiability of stealing property were not opened); no figure by origin group (no source found that gives one). National, not the place's. does_bps is never given: a conduct's own rate in the profile.
sources.culture.origin: PLACE: Tamil Nadu (state), Census of India 2011 (the 2011 census counts Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes; it does not count other castes). groups: Statistical Hand Book of Tamil Nadu 2020-21, table 1.1, Department of Economics and Statistics, Government of Tamil Nadu, https://des.tn.gov.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/areaandpopulation.pdf , OPENED 2026-10-13: total 72,147,030 (rural 37,229,590 + urban 34,917,440); Scheduled Castes 14,438,445 (20.01%); Scheduled Tribes 794,697 (1.10%); Others is the remainder (78.89%). The groups are the census's classes, not birthplace or the place's other communities. same_household_bps: 9418 = 100% less 5.82%, the share of inter-caste marriages in India, IHDS-II 2011-12, as quoted in 'Whose education matters? An analysis of inter-caste marriages in India', Ideas for India, https://www.ideasforindia.in/topics/social-identity/whose-education-matters-an-analysis-of-inter-caste-marriages-in-india , OPENED 2026-10-13 (no Tamil Nadu figure given). National, and by caste (jati), which is finer than these three census classes, so couples across these three classes are rarer than 5.82% (the same share here is probably higher: to confirm). homophily_bps: PLACEHOLDER 5000 (a close tie is half again as likely within a group as by chance). No survey of close ties or friendship by group for this place was found and opened; McPherson, Smith-Lovin and Cook 2001 ('Birds of a feather', Annual Review of Sociology 27) gives the general fact, not this place's figure. CHILDREN: the pages opened do not say which group a child of a mixed couple is counted in (to confirm); the generator's either-parent rule is unverified for this source.
sources.tenancy.rent_share_of_income: PLACEHOLDER: nothing was found. India surveys no household income, and the consumption survey (MoSPI, HCES 2023-24) gives rent only as a share of all urban households' non-food spending, not for renting households and not by band. The bands are borrowed from ke-nakuru-2026's, themselves a placeholder around Nakuru's opened mean of 33.3% of expenditure. To source: NSS 76th round (housing condition), rent of renting households against their monthly consumer expenditure. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Homes by income"): each renting household of a new town draws its share from these bands (evenly within a band; the open band from its lower bound to twice it, at most everything), which gives the rent it carries; households and let homes are matched by it. A target as well: the town's own distribution at the start is reported beside it and is not fitted to it.
sources.support.take_up_bps: pension 30%: TO CONFIRM: a secondary report says about 30% of eligible elderly people in Tamil Nadu receive the old-age pension, the survey behind it unnamed; 34.9 lakh people drew one of twelve state pension schemes in March 2024 against about 1.04 crore people aged 60 and over in 2021, an upper bound of about a third (IMPRI, Tamil Nadu's Old Age Pension Scheme, https://www.impriindia.com/?p=75882, opened 2026-10-12; the population from a search summary). The real pension is for the poor only; the profile's is paid to everyone of its age who claims (its own note says so), so those not drawing it here claim it on the first day and are granted. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/generator.md, "Payments in force"): of those the payment's rule already entitles as the year begins, this share open with it in payment; the rest claim it when they first look, as before.
sources.households.kin_households_most_bps: 10.72%: a PROXY: urban Tamil Nadu households with two or more married couples (Census of India 2011, table HH-5, households by number of married couples, https://censusindia.gov.in/nada/index.php/catalog/8376, opened 2026-10-12). It leaves out extended households of one couple with a parent or other relative, so it is low. The profile states no extended households (its group_bps stands for them). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/households.md, "Taken in"): a ceiling and nothing else: no more households than this hold kin when people with nothing coming in are placed with a household that can carry them.
sources.tenancy.possession: PLACEHOLDERS: the Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act 2017 lets a landlord apply to the Rent Court for eviction where rent is unpaid for two months after a notice (recalled, to confirm); no figure was opened. The two shares of how tenants answer are the same in every profile: stay_past_notice_bps 5000 is a PLACEHOLDER (no figure was found for the share of tenants who stay past a notice for arrears); leave_on_order_bps 5900 is England's, used everywhere: of 16,848 landlord possession orders in January to March 2026, 6,888 repossessions were by county court bailiffs, 41%, so about 59% of those ordered out were gone without one (Ministry of Justice, Mortgage and Landlord Possession Statistics, January to March 2026: opened by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11; a ratio of one quarter's flows, not of one cohort). eviction_notice_days: the notice of the day that whoever carries out a warrant gives the tenant; England's county court bailiffs give 14 days' notice of an eviction (Civil Procedure Rules 83.8A: to confirm, recalled), Germany's Gerichtsvollzieher about three weeks (to confirm); every other place's figure is a PLACEHOLDER (7 days; Ohio 3, within its ten). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/justice.md, "Possession"): published in the town as a law; a landlord gives a notice to vacate under it, applies to the tribunal if the tenant stays, and asks for a warrant if they stay past its order; the tribunal sets a plan or a date by it; the police carry the warrant out. Tenants who answer, and plans (2026-10-12): answer_bps 4000 is a PLACEHOLDER (no figure was found for this place of how many tenants served with an application for possession answer it in writing or attend; it is the middle of the two figures opened for other places: 43% of hearings with the renter or someone for them in Victoria, 39.3% of tenants present in Cleveland, Ohio). plan_consider 'may' is a PLACEHOLDER: the 2017 Act's s 21 was not opened. 2026-10-16: the Act's text is opened (casemine copy; in force from 22 February 2019): eviction where rent is unpaid for two months after a notice of demand, the tenant having a month from the demand to pay (s 21(2)(b)): arrears_days 60 and notice_days 30 agree (the 'recalled, to confirm' is closed); relief by paying arrears with interest, and not again if two consecutive months default in a later year; possession within a month of the order is stated for the owner-occupation ground (s 22), the arrears ground's time was not shown, so possession_days 30 is to confirm. Not modelled, no field: s 23, double the monthly rent as compensation where a tenant stays on after termination.
sources.business.entry_bps_per_year: PLACEHOLDER: no figure for business births in Tamil Nadu or India was found (the research agent's search, 2026-10-11). 10% a year stands in, between the other profiles' figures. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/entry.md, "Starting a business of one"): the generator turns it into a monthly chance for those who could start a business of one (in the labour force, of working age, with the savings for its stock), from the businesses the town has: births a year at this rate, over those people. Most real births are businesses with no employees, which is the only kind that can be started here without premises.
sources.employment.hours: Industrial Disputes Act 1947 ss 25A-25E (lay-off: a worker laid off for want of work is paid compensation of 50% of the basic wage plus dearness allowance, by the employer, for up to 45 days in a year; the compensation does not apply to an establishment of fewer than 50 workers; prior permission to lay off is needed only from 300 workers) and the Industrial Relations Code 2020, in force from 21 November 2025 (to confirm: none opened, read from search results 2026-10-13); the Factories Act 1948 s 51 (48 hours a week; recalled). Here: by notice (none required), 50% of pay for the hours cut from an employer of 50 or more, any spell (the 45-day yearly limit is not modelled). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Hours before heads"): published in the town as a law (law-cutting-hours); a shop or factory over its need cuts everyone's hours to what its trade needs before it lets anyone go, where this says it may, and pays what it owes for the hours cut; a worker reads the employer's paper as the pay agreed. consent_bps 9000 is a PLACEHOLDER (of workers asked to agree to a cut as the alternative to someone being let go, the share who do; no figure found). The employer's own notice of 3 days is ours, so that the paper reaches the worker first. 2026-10-16: the Industrial Relations Code 2020 s 67 (https://courbook.in/industrial-relations-code-2020/section-67, opened): a worker with a year's continuous service, not badli or casual, who is laid off gets 50% of basic wages plus dearness allowance for the days laid off except weekly holidays: pay_bps 5000 agrees; the 45-day limit in a year applies only where worker and employer agree to it (so the note above, which says it applies, is not the Code's text); s 65: ss 67-69 do not apply to an establishment with fewer than 50 workers on average per working day, or to seasonal or intermittent ones; 'industrial establishment' means a factory, mine or plantation, so shops are outside the law and the profile applies it to them (a simplification); a search snippet gave 300 workers for the permission rule, not reconciled with the Code. TN Shops and Establishments Act 1947: 8 hours a day, 48 a week, overtime to 10.5 and 57 hours at double pay (keka.com, a compliance site, secondary): ordinary_week_hours 48 agrees. All four labour codes were notified in force on 21 November 2025 (law-firm summaries).
sources.employment.adjustment: PLACEHOLDERS, the same in every profile, with a sourced shape (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"; docs/research/references.md). smooth_months 3: firms plan production and workforce on smoothed, forecast trade and not on the last period's (Holt, Modigliani, Muth and Simon 1960); no figure for the horizon of a small employer here was found. hiring_cost_weeks 8: what recruiting and training a new worker costs, in weeks of their pay; estimates run from under two weeks to over sixteen (Silva and Toledo 2009; Manning 2011; Blatter, Muehlemann and Schenker 2012; Muehlemann and Leiser 2018: all to confirm, none opened), and none is for this place.
sources.employment.termination: Industrial Disputes Act 1947 s 25F (retrenchment of a workman with a year's continuous service: one month's notice or pay in lieu, and 15 days' average pay for each completed year). It binds industrial establishments; applied here to every employer, which overstates it for small shops (the Tamil Nadu Shops and Establishments Act gives a month's notice and no retrenchment pay) (to confirm: recalled by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-11, the statute not opened). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Adjusting labour"): published in the town as a law; an employer reads it before letting someone go for redundancy (what it would owe is part of what the job costs to end) and pays what it says when the job ends. Service is counted from the start of a run: nobody's earlier years with an employer are known to it. 2026-10-16: the Industrial Relations Code 2020 s 70 now governs retrenchment (https://courtbook.in/industrial-relations-code-2020/section-70, opened): a worker with a year's continuous service gets one month's notice in writing or wages in lieu, and 15 days' average pay for every completed year 'or any part thereof in excess of six months', with notice to the government: the table agrees with s 25F of the 1947 Act cited above; the six-month part-year rule would add up to 15 days and is not in the table.
sources.frictions: Everyday frictions (docs/behaviour/frictions.md): what goes wrong, how often, and how the bodies that hear it work. Read by the generator only for a town whose spec has `living`.
sources.frictions.per_adult_bps_per_year: Of adults, the share who had each kind of problem, a year: half the share who had it in the last two years in World Justice Project, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019 (General Population Poll 2017-18, about 1,000 respondents a country; the summary statistics workbook was opened; national, and for Brazil and Mexico the three largest cities only). landlord: a problem with a landlord over agreements, payments, repairs, deposits or eviction (1.8% in two years; all of it is given to disrepair here, which overstates repairs: the town has no other landlord problem of the kind yet). wages: difficulty obtaining wages or employment benefits agreed in advance (0.7%). bill: major disruption of a utility's supply or incorrect billing (4.9%; all of it is given to wrong bills). benefits: difficulty obtaining public benefits or government assistance (1.0%). goods: a consumer problem (9.3%) less the utility share, since the survey's consumer problems include it (derived; poor professional services are in it too). The generator turns each into a rate for those exposed (a let dwelling, a job, a customer, a claim) with the town's own counts. Halving a two-year share understates a yearly one where people have a problem in both years (to confirm against a yearly survey). 2026-10-16 (not applied): India Employment Report 2024 (IHD and ILO, from PLFS 2022): 40.8% of regular and 51.9% of casual workers earned less than the unskilled agricultural minimum wage, national (Down To Earth, https://www.downtoearth.org.in/news/governance/for-a-decade-earnings-of-regular-salaried-self-employed-indians-have-been-declining-ilo-95290, opened): below the statutory minimum is not pay agreed in advance and not received, a different and much larger construct than the survey's 0.35%. Billing: the Electricity Ombudsman reviewed 385 grievances in 2021-25, 162 about billing (42%) (CAG newsletter above): an appeal outcome, not a rate of wrong bills.
sources.frictions.put_right_on_asking_bps: Asked to put it right, how often the other side does. PLACEHOLDERS, every one: each stands at the share of people with any problem who say it is done and fully resolved (24.5%: World Justice Project, Global Insights on Access to Justice 2019 (General Population Poll 2017-18, about 1,000 respondents a country; the summary statistics workbook was opened; national, and for Brazil and Mexico the three largest cities only)), which is an outcome of everything people tried, not the rate at which the other side agrees when asked: to replace with a figure by kind of problem.

sources.frictions.bill_over_bps: PLACEHOLDER: by how much a wrong bill overstates what was used (30%). No figure was found.
sources.frictions.goods_faulty_share_bps: PLACEHOLDER: of a shopping trip's goods, the share that is faulty when some are (a quarter). No figure was found.

sources.frictions.support: (Until foundations F6 this note also gave a processing time, a placeholder fortnight, and a daily capacity; both are gone: how long a claim takes is the hours of whoever decides it.) wrong_refusal_bps: of claims that qualify, the share wrongly refused. FITTED in the 1,000-person town of the first profile (7% of qualifying claims gives about as many refusals a year as 6% of adults, its survey share with difficulty obtaining public benefits, counting the refusals that are right), and for every other place scaled by its own survey share against that one: a stand-in until a place's own rate of decisions changed on review is found. 2026-10-12: this fit assumed every entitled person claims in the year. A town now opens with the payments its people are already entitled to in force (granted before the year, never decided in it), so it decides fewer claims and refuses fewer (Victoria 37.8 to 24.8 a year). It is NOT re-fitted: that would be fitting an outcome again. Reviews of payments in force, which would add wrong stops, were looked for in this place's law and statistics and no rate of wrong stops per review was found; nothing is built (docs/behaviour/frictions.md, 'Payments in force are not reviewed'; docs/decisions.md, 2026-10-12, 'Reviews of payments in force'). 2026-10-16 (no change): no wrongly-refused or appeal-overturn rate for Tamil Nadu pensions was found; the nearest are a backlog of 74.23 lakh applications pending in July 2023 and 35,37,372 people drawing across 12 schemes in September 2026 (IMPRI, https://www.impriindia.com/?p=75882, a secondary, opened), a backlog and not a rate on review.

sources.frictions.venues: tribunal_days 90: the Rent Court must decide an application within 90 days for most grounds, and within 30 days for two of them (clauses (d) and (g)) (Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act 2017, s 36(6), text at https://www.casemine.com/act/in/67e3e058c818963e4e88c4a0, opened 2026-10-16). It is the law's limit, a ceiling and not a measured time: Tamil Nadu's subordinate civil courts outside Chennai had 657,685 cases pending at the end of 2023 and disposed of 277,287 in the year, a stock-over-flow pendency of about 2.4 years (about 870 days), and the National Consumer Commission's mean is 647 days (Statistical Hand Book of Tamil Nadu 2022-23, table 31.2, https://des.tn.gov.in/sites/default/files/2025-07/31.%20JUDICIAL%20ADMINISTRATION.pdf, decoded; India Justice Report 2026 via moneylife.in): those are all civil cases, not the Rent Court, and no Rent Authority time was found, so the actual wait is probably longer than 90. Replaces the placeholder six weeks. tribunal_fee_hours_of_pay: the fee on an application to the Rent Authority is the fee for an interlocutory application in a civil court (s 41(3), the Tamil Nadu Court-fees and Suits Valuation Act 1955); the rupee amount was not found, so 3 stays a PLACEHOLDER. answer_days 14: the tenant has a month from the landlord's demand notice to pay arrears (s 21(2)(b)), a cure period and not the time to answer a desk: kept as a placeholder. uphold_without_proof_bps: PLACEHOLDER; the Electricity Ombudsman's orders in 2021-25 favoured the consumer in 31 of 162 billing cases (19.1%) (Consumer Action Group, October 2025 newsletter, https://www.cag.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-12/October_Current_News_NL_2025.pdf, opened), a poor map to this share, not applied.
sources.outlook: How people start out in what they trust (docs/behaviour/citizen.md, 'The record'). National figures for India, not the region's: none by region was found. trust: the share with 'a great deal' or 'quite a lot' of confidence in each kind of institution (`government`, `policing`: the police, `courts`, the civil service, banks, the press, labour unions, churches or religious organisations, major companies); people_bps: the share who say most people can be trusted. World Values Survey and European Values Study, joint wave 7 (fieldwork 2017 to 2022), as Our World in Data publishes it (ourworldindata.org/grapher/trust-state-institutions-wvs, trust-organizations-wvs, self-reported-trust-attitudes), opened 2026-10-11 through a tool that returns a page's figures in summary: to confirm against the survey's own tables. The share is read as the mean level of trust a person starts with, which is a simplification (a share above a threshold is not a mean). Not stated, so the citizen's own placeholders apply (to source: the survey's question on freedom of choice and control over one's life, its mean and spread, needs the microdata): how much control over their lives people feel (outlook.agency).
sources.outlook.residence: PLACEHOLDER: no figure for how long people have lived at their address was found for India on a page opened. Borrowed from Australia's (the only place whose figures were opened), for lack of any: ABS, 2021 Census, 'Population movement in Australia' (released 8 November 2022; abs.gov.au/articles/population-movement-australia), opened 2026-10-11: 53.1% of the population lived at the same address five years before the Census; 14.3% changed address within Australia in the year before; 0.7% had lived overseas a year before. Bands here: under 1 year = 14.3 + 0.7 = 15.0%; 1 to under 5 = the rest (31.9%); 5 and over = 53.1%. They are built from the one-year and five-year mobility rates, so the 1 to under 5 band is the remainder, and the 5-and-over share is the share at the same address five years earlier (population aged 5 and over, not adults only). National figures, not Victoria's: the Victoria figures were not found on an opened page. The open band is read as 5 to 15 years by the generator. India's own are probably different (to source: Census or housing-survey tables of years since moving in). 2026-10-16: Census of India 2011, table D-02 (migrants by duration of residence, by state) is the source to use for Tamil Nadu urban; it was found in the catalogue but not opened, so the borrowed bands stand.
sources.outlook.job_tenure: PLACEHOLDER: (how long employed people have been with their current employer, for their starting attachment to the trade) no job tenure figure for India was found (tenure is rarely published there, and the OECD dataset does not cover it). Borrowed from Brazil's, the nearest case with a large informal and own-account labour force whose figures were opened: OECD, 'Employment by job tenure intervals' (dataset OECD.ELS.SAE DSD_TENURE@DF_TENURE_FREQ, measure TENURE_EMP, share of employment by time with the current employer; both sexes, all ages), national figures for Brazil, 2024; read from the OECD SDMX API (sdmx.oecd.org/public/rest/data/OECD.ELS.SAE,DSD_TENURE@DF_TENURE_FREQ) on 2026-10-11, the response opened and the figures copied: under 1 year, 1 to under 3, 3 to under 5, 5 to under 10, 10 and over. National, not the region's: none by region was found. It covers the employed (employees and the self-employed), where a person's tenure is the time in the present job. The open band (10 and over) is read as 10 to 30 years by the generator. The shares sum to 99.9 to 100 in the source and are scaled to 10000. Borrowed here for lack of any figure of India's own; people there are likely to have shorter tenures in informal work, and longer in farming.
sources.employment.registered_bps: MoSPI, Periodic Labour Force Survey, Annual Report July 2023 to June 2024, table 36 (https://www.mospi.gov.in/sites/default/files/publication_reports/AnnualReport_PLFS2023-24L2.pdf; opened and read by a research agent for this work, 2026-10-09): of regular wage or salaried employees outside agriculture in urban Tamil Nadu, 46.2% are not eligible for any specified social security benefit (48.5% have no written job contract, 40.3% no paid leave), so 53.8% are taken as registered. For regular employees only; applied to jobs by the day as well, which overstates their registration (casual labourers have next to none). HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Jobs an employer does not register"): each employer of a kind registers this share of its own jobs; a job outside it is paid whole, nothing is withheld and no report names the worker. The same share is given for shops, factories and construction because the source divides employees by status, not by kind of employer (its rates by activity count own-account workers too, and are not used). Nothing inspects: the share is a stated fact of the place. In this profile the law takes nothing from pay at these wages and no charge is reported worker by worker, so registering a job or not changes no payment here: the provident fund and the state insurance, which are what registration brings in fact, are not in the profile (to add, with their rates).
sources.employment.casual_bps: The same report, table 19 (opened likewise): of workers in urban Tamil Nadu (usual status), 52.9% are regular wage or salaried, 17.8% casual labour, 29.3% self-employed. Casual labour is so 17.8 of 70.7, 25.18% of those who work for an employer. HOW IT IS USED (docs/behaviour/firms.md, "Work by the day"): that share of each employer's jobs is by the day. The same share for each kind of employer: the table by industry was not opened (construction's is certainly higher and a shop's lower: to restate by kind).
sources.employment.day_wage: MoSPI, PLFS calendar year 2024, urban Tamil Nadu, average daily wage earnings from casual labour other than public works, persons: 617.71 rupees (the figure this profile's construction wage already rests on; via the eSankhyiki data server, opened by the profile's author 2026-10-08). The PLFS annual report 2023-24, table 39, gives 626, 629, 597 and 638 rupees for the four quarters (opened by a research agent, 2026-10-09). sources.employment.own_account: [MIXED] Share: the same PLFS report, table 19: in urban Tamil Nadu 25.2% of workers are own-account workers or employers (the table gives the two together; helpers in a household enterprise, 4.1%, are left out). It is means-tested to the poor; the structure pays every person from the age, so this overstates coverage (gap). Paid monthly, so every_days is 30. [The payment to those out of work:] None: India has no general unemployment benefit (the Employees' State Insurance scheme's Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana pays only some insured workers, and the rural employment guarantee gives up to 100 days of paid work a household, ₹319 a day in Tamil Nadu in 2024-25, which is work, not a transfer: Ministry of Rural Development, as reported; to confirm). The amount is 0, the closest the structure allows. Women heads of household in Tamil Nadu receive ₹1,000 a month (Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thogai, from September 2023; to confirm): not expressible (gap). UN-FOLDED: the payment of nought that stood for no payment to the unemployed is gone (this note: India has no general unemployment benefit), so nobody claims one and none is counted. STAND-IN KEPT: the pension is still paid to everyone from 60. It is means-tested to the poor; that can now be said (`who.income_under`: the household's income as the claimant declares it), but this note gives no income line, so none is set. The payment to women heads of household could be said as a household's payment; a rule by sex is not built.

EXPRESSED NOW, from this note: the rebate that leaves income up to ₹12,00,000 untaxed (no tax is due where the taxable income is that or less), and the Health and Education Cess of 4% of the tax, a charge on the tax. The levy of nought that stood for no levy is gone. Not expressed: the standard deduction (the note gives no figure for it: the field is a deduction, `base.less`), and the marginal relief just above the rebate's line.
sources.public_finance.returns: [RECALLED, to confirm] Income Tax Department: tax deducted from salary is deposited by the 7th of the following month (March's by 30 April), the quarterly statement being Form 24Q; the cess is part of the TDS. The department's pages returned an access error; seen on secondary sites. EPF and ESI (due the 15th) are not charges in this profile.
sources.public_finance.grants_per_resident_per_y: PLACEHOLDER, ₹1,500 a resident a year: Tamil Nadu's devolution to local bodies on the State Finance Commission's recommendation and Union grants under the Fifteenth Finance Commission (not opened, to source).

sources.public_finance.rates_instalments: Tamil Nadu District Municipalities Act 1920 and Town Panchayats Act 1998: property tax is payable half-yearly (by 30 September and 31 March; to confirm the sections).
sources.public_finance.rates_due_days: Placeholder: an instalment falls due 30 days after its notice.
sources.public_finance.rates_penalty_interest_bp: Tamil Nadu local bodies charge 2% a month on unpaid property tax, 24% a year (not opened, to confirm).

The note is its author's, as written.) 0: no landfill levy was found in Tamil Nadu (the Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 provide for user fees and spot fines, not a levy per tonne; to confirm).

sources.services.asset_life_years: PLACEHOLDER carried over: a park or civic building wears out in 15 years without upkeep.
sources.services.upkeep_hours_per_week_per_asset: PLACEHOLDER carried over: a crew member's half a day a week keeps a park or the hall up.
sources.services.complain_bps: PLACEHOLDER carried over: the chance a week that a household whose waste has gone two weeks uncollected writes to the town. A complaint rate is to be sourced (Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister's Helpline is the channel).
sources.public_service.wage_per_pay_period: [SECONDARY] Tamil Nadu Ministerial Service Junior Assistant (also used in town panchayats): Pay Matrix Level 8, Rs 19,500-71,900 a month (7th Pay Commission scale, as listed in TNPSC notifications seen in search results, not opened in full). A mid-scale basic of about Rs 25,000 plus dearness allowance and house rent allowance gives roughly Rs 38,000 gross a month (the DA and HRA rates are estimated, to confirm). x 12 / 26 = about Rs 17,500 a fortnight = 1,750,000 paise. Rounded; no false precision. 2026-10-16 (not applied): Pay Matrix Level 8 starts at Rs 19,500 (cell 10, about ten years, Rs 25,400), dearness allowance 60% from 1 January 2026 (Tamil Nadu government announcement via Angel One, opened; the matrix from indianpaycalculator.in, a calculator site, secondary): basic plus DA at cell 10 is Rs 40,640 and gross about Rs 41,300 to 42,100, which over 26 fortnights is Rs 19,100 to 19,400, 9 to 11% above 17,500; that Level 8 is the junior assistant's rests on search snippets only (the TNPSC notice refused connection), so it stays. DA at 60% applies to the officer, teacher and doctor wage placeholders as well, not recomputed here.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.administra: [PLACEHOLDER] 1.5 FTE per 1,000, estimated from the Tamil Nadu Town Panchayat sanction rule of one bill collector per 3,000 bills (G.O. seen in search results, tn.gov.in/dtp, not opened) plus a small clerical and registry staff of a town panchayat office; works crew and elected members excluded. To confirm against a Directorate of Town Panchayats staffing pattern.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.courts: [PLACEHOLDER] 0.1 FTE per 1,000: India has about 21 judges per million people (Law Commission and Supreme Court figures, from memory, to confirm), and a court carries perhaps 4 to 5 registry staff per judge; the first-instance civil court serving a town is shared with its district. Estimated, not opened.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.oversight: [PLACEHOLDER] 0.03 FTE per 1,000 for ombudsman and consumer-protection bodies together: a District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has a president, two members and a handful of staff for a district of millions; Tamil Nadu has no general ombudsman of note. Estimated, to confirm.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.elections: [PLACEHOLDER] 0.03 FTE per 1,000: permanent election staff (a district election office and the State Election Commission) are few; most polling work is done by seconded staff. Estimated, not opened.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.land_regis: [PLACEHOLDER] 0.05 FTE per 1,000: a Sub-Registrar office in Tamil Nadu (Registration Department) has a sub-registrar and about 5 to 8 staff for a sub-district of roughly 100,000+ people. Estimated, to confirm.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.press: [PLACEHOLDER] 0.05 FTE per 1,000: a Tamil-language daily's local editorial desk (a reporter or two per taluk of 200,000 to 400,000 people). Estimated from the shape of local news bureaus, not sourced.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.banking: [PLACEHOLDER] 1.5 FTE per 1,000: Indian scheduled commercial banks employ roughly 1.5 million staff for about 1.4 billion people (about 1 per 1,000; Reserve Bank of India, Statistical Tables, from memory, to confirm); urban Tamil Nadu is better served than the average, so a little above it. 2026-10-16: scheduled commercial banks employed 1,900,697 in 2024-25 nationally, about 1.3 per 1,000 (RBI, Statistical Tables Relating to Banks in India 2024-25, seen in a search summary: SUMMARY-ONLY); the 1.5 here sits 15% above national as its note intends.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.utilities: [PLACEHOLDER] 1.5 FTE per 1,000: TANGEDCO/TNPDCL and its distribution staff run to roughly 80,000 to 90,000 people for about 78 million (about 1.1 per 1,000, from memory, to confirm) plus water board operations; the figure rounds up for the water side. 2026-10-16 (not applied): Tamil Nadu Energy Department White Paper (25 June 2026): 74,714 of 140,635 posts filled across TNPDCL, TANTRANSCO, TNPGCL and TNGECL over 77.5 million people = 0.96 per 1,000 (0.74 distribution alone), regular staff only, generation and transmission included (decoded PDF, opened); about 13% under the 1.1 for electricity: not changed.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.union: [PLACEHOLDER] 0.1 FTE per 1,000: full-time union officers are a small fraction of members; Tamil Nadu's trade unions (CITU, AITUC, LPF and others) have many part-time office holders. A rough estimate, not sourced.
sources.public_service.licences.payment_system: [PLACEHOLDER] 15,000 paise (Rs 150) per resident per year: a core-banking and payment platform costs a small Indian bank on the order of Rs 100 to 300 per customer a year (vendor licence and processing; estimated, no source opened, to confirm). 2026-10-16: no per-account price found; the Reserve Bank's scheme for urban co-operative banks pays Rs 15,000 per branch per month for core banking (taxheal.com, summary), which cannot be turned into a per-resident figure.
sources.public_service.staff_per_1000.property_m: [PLACEHOLDER] Carried over unchanged to every profile: property managers (people who run let homes for their owners) at about one to every 100 to 150 let homes is an industry rule of thumb (to confirm, not opened); a town here has about 380 homes for 1,000 people, so about 3 per 1,000 residents. A manager looks after the letting offices of several landlords.
sources.public_service.appointed_by: [PLACEHOLDER] Who fills the post of a public body when none of its own staff is left: the town's council, which seconds one of its own staff to it, as a local government assigns officers to bodies it runs. Real places mostly give these appointments to a state body, a minister or a board, none of which the town models, so the council stands in for them (to confirm per place). Bodies run on their own account (the bank, the union, the paper, landlords, shops) are not covered: their owners or members would appoint, and no owner's or member's office exists to do it.
sources.unions.membership_bps: PLACEHOLDERS, to source: Labour Bureau, Trade Union Statistics (the last verified-membership report is for 2012-13); most workers are informal and unorganised (PLFS 2023-24 informal share; to confirm). Government employees' associations are the most organised, retail and construction the least. `other`, the overall rate.
sources.unions.dues_per_month: PLACEHOLDER, ₹30 a month: trade union dues in India are nominal (the Trade Unions Act 1926 sets a minimum subscription of 25 paise a month for registered unions; to confirm).
sources.unions.resignation_notice_days: Trade Unions Act 1926 (to confirm the section): a member may resign on notice in writing to the secretary, effective on receipt: 0 days.
sources.unions.claim_margin_bps: Placeholder carried over: a union claims the year's rise in prices and 2% more.
sources.unions.meeting_every_days: Placeholder: a members' meeting a month.
sources.unions.teaching: The union movement's claim, in words (content for belief). Its members hold it at the start.
sources.groups.kinds: PLACEHOLDERS: the kinds of social group (sport, religion, arts and culture, hobbies, community clubs); no Indian national survey of group membership was found. Women's self-help groups (Tamil Nadu Corporation for Development of Women, Mahalir Thittam) and temple committees are central in Tamil Nadu and have no kind of their own here (gap). How often each meets, and for how long: placeholders.
sources.groups.per_kind_per_1000_people: Placeholder: one group of each kind for every 1,000 people.
sources.groups.taking_part_bps: PLACEHOLDER carried over (40%): the share of adults who belong to a group at the start and go to its gatherings. No Indian survey figure found (World Values Survey India wave, 'active membership', to source).
sources.groups.leave_notice_days: Placeholder: a member may leave a club or congregation at once.
sources.groups.kinds.teaching: What a group asks people to hold, in its words: content for belief to attach to. The congregation's stands for the town's faiths together (Hindu, Christian and Muslim; one congregation per town is a simplification), worded as belief in a divine power because they are not one doctrine.
sources.groups.kinds.held_at_start_bps: 97%: the share of Indians who believe in God (Pew Research Center, 'Religion in India: Tolerance and Segregation', 2021; to confirm). Census of India 2011, Tamil Nadu: Hindus 87.6%, Christians 6.1%, Muslims 5.9% (to confirm). At the start, the congregation's members hold its teaching strongly, and others up to this share hold it less.
sources.elections: Tamil Nadu Panchayats and Municipalities Acts: local bodies are elected for five years, by first-past-the-post in single-member wards; the town panchayat's chairperson is chosen by the councillors (Tamil Nadu State Election Commission, urban local body elections of 19 February 2022). This town elects its leader directly (a liberty). turnout: 74.68% in town panchayats at the 2022 urban local body elections (State Election Commission, as reported by The News Minute, 'TN urban polls: Overall voter turnout 60.7%'; The News Minute's article of 20 February 2022 was opened and says the town panchayats recorded 74.68% and the municipalities 68.22%, citing the Tamil Nadu State Election Commission; the SEC's own site (tnsec.tn.gov.in) could not be reached). Voting is not compulsory. stand_bps: placeholder, 2%. news_readers_bps: placeholder (Reuters Institute Digital News Report: India, to source).
sources.health: The clinic stands for the town's health system (a primary health centre or taluk hospital, and the private clinics and hospital it refers to; a liberty: a town of a few thousand has a primary health centre, not a hospital). doctors_per_1000: 130,898 registered allopathic doctors in Tamil Nadu (Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, reply in Parliament, 2024, as found by search) at 80% availability (the Ministry's own assumption) over 77.546 million people (Technical Group on Population Projections 2011-2036, Tamil Nadu, 1 March 2026, Table T-17, opened): 1.35 per 1,000 (neither opened, to confirm). doctor_wage_per_pay_period: PLACEHOLDER, about ₹85,000 a month for an Assistant Surgeon in the Tamil Nadu Medical Services (pay matrix plus dearness allowance; to source). consult_minutes, seek_care_bps, treats and off_work_severities: placeholders carried over (the conditions here are hospital-level; in India much care is out of pocket at private providers and the poorest delay care: gap).
sources.education: school_ages: children start Class 1 at five or six and the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act 2009 makes school compulsory from 6 to 14; the town's school runs to Class 12, at 17 (Tamil Nadu School Education Department). students_per_teacher: 23 for Tamil Nadu in 2024-25 (UDISE+ 2024-25, Ministry of Education, opened via MoSPI eSankhyiki data server (mcp.mospi.gov.in), opened 2026-10-08; 24 in 2023-24; by level, 2024-25: primary 20, upper primary 18, secondary 12, higher secondary 21). school_days_per_year: 210 working days (Tamil Nadu School Education Department's academic calendar; to confirm). hours_per_day: about 6 (placeholder; Tamil Nadu schools run about 9:20 to 4:00). teacher_wage_per_pay_period: PLACEHOLDER, about ₹45,000 a month for a government school teacher (Tamil Nadu pay scales plus dearness allowance; to source). attainment: shaped by NFHS-5 Tamil Nadu: women literate 84.0%, men 90.7%; women with 10 or more years of schooling 56.6%, men 59.1% (IIPS, NFHS-5 State Fact Sheet, Tamil Nadu, indicators 14-17); the split between levels is a placeholder (to source from PLFS 2023-24, general educational level, Tamil Nadu), as years of schooling. return_per_year_bps: about 8% (Duraisamy 2002, 'Changes in returns to education in India, 1983-94', Economics of Education Review 21; estimates run 6-10%; to confirm), taken as productivity (Mincer 1974) and applied linearly in the time a task takes. max_years: the skill scale's top (placeholder).
sources.round: Working hours 9 to 5, six days a week (Tamil Nadu Shops and Establishments Act: 48 hours over six days; a liberty: the actual day is often 9 to 7 with a long break; not modelled); school 9 to 4 (placeholder; Tamil Nadu schools run about 9:20 to 4:00). Travel: off the roads, a 25 m cell on foot in about 18 seconds (walking about 1.4 m/s: Bohannon 1997); on a road, about 3 seconds (a two-wheeler or auto-rickshaw at about 30 km/h in a town; most small-town trips are by two-wheeler, bicycle or on foot; placeholder); slower across water, wetland and bush (placeholders). Roads: the town builds toward buildings more than three cells (75 m) from one (placeholder), within a roads budget scaled from the other profile's by the ratio of shop wages (3.02).
sources.ownership: house_owner_bps: Census of India 2011, Table HL-04 'Households by ownership status of the census houses', Tamil Nadu (opened): of 8,929,104 urban households 5,130,112 (57.5%) own their house, 3,590,179 (40.2%) rent (rural: 90.5% own); a census town is urban, so the urban share is used. Flats here are all rented (a liberty). mortgage_bps_by_age: PLACEHOLDER; few Indian homeowners hold a mortgage (most build in stages from savings and family loans); NSS 78th round (2020-21) and RBI data on housing loans are to be used (to source). mortgage_payment_per_month: PLACEHOLDER, ₹8,000 (about a ₹9 lakh loan over 15 years at 8%). mortgage_rate_bps: PLACEHOLDER, 8.0%, the order of banks' home-loan rates after the 2025 repo cuts (to confirm). mortgage_years_left: placeholder. market: deposit_bps 10%: the RBI's loan-to-value ceiling is 90% for home loans up to ₹30 lakh (RBI Master Circular on Housing Finance, 2022; to confirm); costs_bps 9%: Tamil Nadu stamp duty of 7% and registration fee of 2% (Registration Department, Tamil Nadu; to confirm); mortgage_months 240: placeholder; buy_bps_per_month, relist_days, cut_bps and floor_bps: placeholders carried over (Merlo and Ortalo-Magne 2004).
sources.utilities: Water: PLACEHOLDER, 70 litres a person a day, the Tamil Nadu Water Supply and Drainage Board's supply norm for a town panchayat (TWAD Board design norms; recalled, not opened, to confirm); tariff PLACEHOLDERS ₹5 a kilolitre and ₹150 a quarter of service charges (many Tamil Nadu town panchayats charge a flat monthly fee; to source); bills go to owners. The river's inflow, flow and losses are placeholders carried over, sized so a small town's draw is a small share of a modest river's water. Energy (electricity): a Tamil Nadu household uses about 4 kWh a day (PLACEHOLDER; TNPDCL consumer data to source); Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission, Order on tariff subsidy for FY 2025-26 (27 March 2025; archived copy of tnerc.tn.gov.in, opened): for domestic LT tariff I-A from 1 July 2024, a consumer using up to 500 units in two months pays nothing for the first 100 units, 235 paise a unit for 101-200, 470 paise for 201-400, and 630 paise for 401-500, the Government of Tamil Nadu paying the rest of the approved tariff (480 paise a unit and more) as a subsidy. The free block cannot be expressed: price_per_kwh 181 paise is the average a household using 4 kWh a day (244 units in a two-month bill) pays under the schedule below: first 100 units nil, 101-200 units 235 paise, 201-400 units 470 paise: (100 x 2.35 + 44 x 4.70) / 244 = 1.81 rupees (derived; a household using less pays less, and many pay nothing); supply_per_day 0 (the fixed charge of ₹107 per kW per month for domestic consumers is met by the Government's subsidy in the same order). grid_price_per_kwh: PLACEHOLDER; TNPDCL's cost of supply is above its domestic tariff and the State pays the gap as a subsidy (₹173 billion to TNPDCL in 2026-27, powerline.net.in, 1 May 2026): not expressible, so the retailer's purchase price is placed below its sale price (gap). grid_emissions_g_per_kwh: 710 g, about India's grid average emission factor (Central Electricity Authority, CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector, about 0.71-0.73 t/MWh; not opened, to confirm).
sources.climate: Weather drawn for each run (docs/behaviour/weather.md). rain_by_month_bps: Tamil Nadu gets about 52-55% of its rain in the Northeast Monsoon (October to December), about 30-32% in the Southwest Monsoon (June to September), November the wettest month (India Meteorological Department normals; Tamil Nadu agricultural university summaries for Thanjavur, as found by search; the monthly normals were not opened, to confirm). The month-by-month split (October 19%, November 21%, December 13%; June 5%, July 6%, August 9%, September 11%; January to May 16% together) is a PLACEHOLDER shaped on those shares; river flow is taken to follow rain. storm_*: PLACEHOLDERS: a heavy-rain spell (cyclone or depression, as in November 2015, December 2023, November 2024) in about one month in ten; the structure's storm chance is the same every month, but in Tamil Nadu it comes in October to December (a gap). drought_*: PLACEHOLDERS: about one year in ten starts a drought of six to eighteen months at 40% of usual inflow (the Northeast Monsoon failed badly in 2016-17; to source). Heatwaves: PLACEHOLDERS: summer is April to June, heat waves are rarer on the coast but hit the interior; three to five days, about one summer week in 17. Heat units and heat illness: carried over from the other profile (its source is Victorian, not Indian). warning_lead_days: IMD's early warnings a couple of days ahead (placeholder).
sources.hazards: Floods (world-expansion 7.3), PLACEHOLDERS carried over, sized against the river as modelled: it spills over its banks past 12,000 kL a cell, 30% of the excess a day; a building floods with water above 300 kL on its cell; wetland (tanks; Tamil Nadu has tens of thousands of irrigation tanks) soaks up 500 kL a cell a day. Tamil Nadu's recorded floods: Chennai 2015, Cauvery delta 2018 (Cyclone Gaja), Thoothukudi and Tirunelveli December 2023, Cyclone Fengal 2024 (Tamil Nadu State Disaster Management Authority; to source). Councils run relief centres: here the town hall.
sources.crime: Crime (world-expansion 7.2), deliberately rare and driven by circumstance only (need and opportunity, and the chance of being caught: Becker 1968; Cohen and Felson 1979), never by any group. take_bps_per_month_in_need, caught_bps_reckoned and take_quantity: placeholders. detection_bps: PLACEHOLDER carried over, 20% (National Crime Records Bureau, Crime in India, Tamil Nadu theft chargesheeting rate; not opened, to source). police_per_1000: PLACEHOLDER, 1.5: about 150 police per 100,000 people in Tamil Nadu (Bureau of Police Research and Development, Data on Police Organisations; not opened, to confirm). officer_wage_per_pay_period: PLACEHOLDER, about ₹30,000 a month for a Grade I police constable (Tamil Nadu Police pay matrix plus dearness allowance; to confirm). investigation_hours: placeholder.
sources.justice: The tribunal stands for the Rent Authority and the Labour Court (Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act 2017; Industrial Relations Code 2020). hearing_after_days: PLACEHOLDER, four months to a first hearing (the National Judicial Data Grid shows long pendency in Indian subordinate courts; the figure is a guess, to source). pay_within_days: placeholder. challenge_bps and apply_bps: placeholders, lower than the other profile's, because few tenants or workers in the informal economy go to a court or the labour office (to source, e.g. Labour Bureau reports on disputes). apply_after_days: a month's wait for payment first (placeholder). Enforcement of an unpaid money order by attachment of the debtor's bank account (Code of Civil Procedure 1908, Order XXI; to confirm).
sources.nature: Nature (docs/design/world-expansion.md 2). cell_m: a cell is a 25 m lot. The landscape is a Cauvery-delta type: mostly paddy farmland (58%), tanks and wetland (7%), scrub (12%), grassland (15%) and little woodland (8%); Tamil Nadu's recorded forest and tree cover is about a fifth to a quarter of the state, mostly in the hills (India State of Forest Report 2023, Forest Survey of India; not opened, to confirm), so the plains share is lower. The shares, margin_cells, block_cells, woodland_patches, the covers' succession (cleared land to grassland in a year; scrub to woodland in about 30), the pollution figures, survey_hours_per_ha and survey_staff are PLACEHOLDERS. spin_up_years: nature is run alone this long before the start, so it begins in its own balance.
sources.nature.species: Real species of the region; every ecology figure (density_per_ha, home_range_ha, growth, mortality, dispersal, min_viable, detection, barriers, tolerance) is a PLACEHOLDER from general natural history, to source from field studies. IUCN Red List status and protection: Indian star tortoise (Geochelone elegans), Vulnerable, dry scrub and grassland, Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972 Schedule IV, CITES Appendix I (listed here); Indian peafowl (Pavo cristatus), Least Concern, India's national bird, Schedule I; Indian pond heron (Ardeola grayii), Least Concern, wetlands, paddy and tanks; smooth-coated otter (Lutrogale perspicillata), Vulnerable, rivers and tanks, sensitive to pollution (listed here). The statuses are from memory of the IUCN Red List and not opened (to confirm).
